metas.name: The Act of Killing
metas.description:
Captures impunity as performance. Indonesian mass killers, never punished and locally celebrated, gleefully re-stage their killings as Hollywood genres, until one man's body reacts before his conscience does.

A documentary which challenges former Indonesian death-squad leaders to reenact their mass-killings in whichever cinematic genres they wish, including classic Hollywood crime scenarios and lavish musical numbers.

metas.name: Waltz with Bashir
metas.description:
Captures a soldier's memory with a hole in it. Animated interviews as the director tries to recover what he did in Beirut in 1982, ending with footage that breaks the animation open.

An Israeli film director interviews fellow veterans of the 1982 invasion of Lebanon to reconstruct his own memories of his term of service in that conflict.

metas.name: The Death of Stalin
metas.description:
Captures absolute power as petty, terrified men improvising. Stalin drops dead and his inner circle plot, flatter and panic in the same breath — very funny, and people keep being shot between jokes.

Moscow, 1953. After being in power for nearly 30 years, Soviet dictator, Joseph Vissarionovich Stalin, takes ill and quickly dies. Now the members of the Council of Ministers scramble for power.

metas.name: Lawrence of Arabia
metas.description:
Captures a man inventing himself at desert scale. Nearly four hours: the landscape is a character, and so is the gap between the legend being built and the person inside it.

The story of T.E. Lawrence, the English officer who successfully united and led the diverse, often warring, Arab tribes during World War I in order to fight the Turks.

metas.name: Summer of Soul
metas.description:
Captures a community's archive left in a basement for 50 years. The 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival — Stevie Wonder, Nina Simone, Mahalia Jackson, Sly Stone — in footage almost nobody saw.

Documentary about the legendary 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival which celebrated African-American music and culture and promoted Black pride and unity.

metas.name: 20 Feet from Stardom
metas.description:
Captures the voices you know best belonging to people you can't name. Backup singers for the Stones, Springsteen and Sting — huge talent, a career spent three steps behind someone else.

Backup singers live in a world that lies just beyond the spotlight. Their voices bring harmony to the biggest bands in popular music, but we've had no idea who these singers are or what lives they lead, until now.

metas.name: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford
metas.description:
Captures celebrity worship in 1882. A famous outlaw ageing and paranoid, and a young admirer who memorised his life from dime novels and moves into his orbit — slow, golden, narrated like a history book.

Robert Ford, who has idolized Jesse James since childhood, tries hard to join the resurgent gang of the Missouri outlaw, but gradually becomes resentful of the bandit leader.

metas.name: Apollo 13
metas.description:
Captures competence under constraint. An explosion in space, and the film becomes people in rooms with slide rules solving the next physical problem before the air runs out — the opposite of lone-hero cinema.

NASA must devise a strategy to return Apollo 13 to Earth safely after the spacecraft undergoes massive internal damage putting the lives of the three astronauts on board in jeopardy.

metas.name: First Man
metas.description:
Captures the Moon landing from inside a grieving, taciturn man. Armstrong as an engineer who can land anything except in his own family's pain; the flights are rattling, cramped and procedural.

A look back at the life of astronaut Neil Armstrong and the legendary space mission that led him to become the first man to walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969.

metas.name: When We Were Kings
metas.description:
Captures Ali as a political and verbal artist at his peak. The Rumble in the Jungle, Zaire 1974: training footage, a music festival, Mobutu's stadium, and Ali talking everyone, including himself, into belief.

Boxing documentary on the 1974 world heavyweight championship bout between defending champion, George Foreman, and the underdog challenger, Muhammad Ali.

metas.name: All the President's Men
metas.description:
Captures journalism as shoe leather. Watergate as phone calls, parking garages, notebooks and editors asking 'what else do you have?' — verification repeated until a presidency moves.

"The Washington Post" reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein uncover the details of the Watergate scandal that leads to President Richard Nixon's resignation.

metas.name: Spotlight
metas.description:
Captures an investigation as a team slowly realising the size of the room they're in. Boston Globe reporters, church abuse, sealed records, survivors telling it plainly — no heroics beyond persistence.

The true story of how the Boston Globe uncovered the massive scandal of child molestation and cover-up within the local Catholic Archdiocese, shaking the entire Catholic Church to its core.

metas.name: Zodiac
metas.description:
Captures obsession with a case that will not close. San Francisco, years of codes, files, basements and false certainties; the killer fades and the men who chased him are what's left damaged.

Between 1968 and 1983, a San Francisco cartoonist becomes an amateur detective obsessed with tracking down the Zodiac Killer, an unidentified individual who terrorizes Northern California with a killing spree.

metas.name: Silence
metas.description:
Captures faith tested by other people's suffering, not your own. Jesuit priests in 17th-century Japan, where Christians are tortured to make them apostatise and God does not answer — Scorsese's quietest, most unresolved film.

In the 17th century, two Portuguese Jesuit priests travel to Japan in an attempt to locate their mentor, who is rumored to have committed apostasy, and to propagate Catholicism.

metas.name: The Colour of Pomegranates
metas.description:
Captures a poet's life as a series of icons instead of events. An Armenian troubadour rendered in tableaux — books, blood, grapes, lace — with almost no dialogue and no interest in explaining itself.

The life of the Armenian poet Sayat-Nova, from childhood to death: his spiritual journey, artistic endeavors, and inner conflicts within the cultural and historical context of Armenia. Hailed as revolutionary by Mikhail Vartanov.

metas.name: Russian Ark
metas.description:
Captures 300 years of history in one held breath. A single unbroken shot drifts through the Hermitage, past czars and ballrooms, with the camera as a ghost nobody quite sees.

A 19th century French aristocrat, notorious for his scathing memoirs about life in Russia, travels through the Russian State Hermitage Museum and encounters historical figures from the last 200+ years.

metas.name: Quo Vadis, Aida?
metas.description:
Captures catastrophe processed as procedure. Srebrenica, 1995, through a UN translator moving names between lists, gates and buses — horror administered in queues and stamps, with everyone following protocol.

Aida is a translator for the UN in the small town of Srebrenica. When the Serbian army takes over the town, her family is among the thousands of citizens looking for shelter in the UN camp.

metas.name: The Zone of Interest
metas.description:
Captures evil as a domestic soundscape. The Höss family gardens, swims and hosts lunches on the other side of the Auschwitz wall; you see almost nothing of the camp and hear it in every scene.

The commandant of Auschwitz and his wife strive to build a dream life for their family in a house next to the camp.

metas.name: Night and Fog
metas.description:
Captures the Holocaust through the quiet, empty camps a decade later rather than footage of the killing itself: grass growing over atrocity, and how quickly a society decides to move on. Resnais' 32-minute essay remains documentary's foundational act of memory.

The history of Nazi Germany's death camps of the Final Solution and the hellish world of dehumanization and death contained inside.

metas.name: Chronicle of a Summer
metas.description:
Captures the moment documentary stopped pretending the camera wasn't in the room. Rouch and Morin ask Parisians 'Are you happy?', then film themselves arguing over whether the answers were real — cinéma vérité examining its own honesty.

A documentary about the everyday lives of ordinary Parisians, done in the style of cinéma vérité.

metas.name: Hearts and Minds
metas.description:
Captures how a country talks itself into a war and then can't talk itself out of the damage. Vietnam told by everyone it passed through — generals, pilots, Vietnamese villagers, American POWs and grieving parents.

A startling and courageous landmark documentary that unflinchingly confronted the United States' involvement in Vietnam at the height of the controversy that surrounded it.

metas.name: Shoah
metas.description:
Captures memory itself as evidence. Nine and a half hours with not one frame of archival footage — only survivors, bystanders and perpetrators talking in the present tense, in the places where it happened. The most demanding film in the collection.

Claude Lanzmann's epic documentary recounts the story of the Holocaust through interviews with witnesses - perpetrators as well as survivors.

metas.name: The Fog of War
metas.description:
Captures a brilliant man half-confessing to catastrophe. Robert McNamara, architect of Vietnam escalation, now in his eighties, lays out eleven lessons from his life in power — you decide whether the other half is honesty or self-defence.

The story of America as seen through the eyes of the former Secretary of Defense under President John F. Kennedy and President Lyndon B. Johnson, Robert McNamara.

metas.name: I Am Not Your Negro
metas.description:
Captures a writer so precise that footage from decades after his death still fits his sentences. James Baldwin's unfinished manuscript on the murders of Medgar Evers, Malcolm X and Martin Luther King, read over a century of American images.

Writer James Baldwin tells the story of race in modern America with his unfinished novel, Remember This House.

metas.name: Apollo 11
metas.description:
Captures the sheer procedural calm of the Moon landing. Rebuilt entirely from restored 70mm footage and audio — no narration, no talking heads — just thousands of people doing small jobs correctly until a man is standing on the Moon.

A look at the Apollo 11 mission to land on the moon led by commander Neil Armstrong and pilots Buzz Aldrin and Mike Collins.

metas.name: The Look of Silence
metas.description:
Captures confrontation inverted: Adi, whose brother was murdered in Indonesia's 1965 purges, visits the killers under cover of eye exams and asks about the killings to their faces — no shouting, only unbearable quiet where they still hold power.

A family that survived the genocide in Indonesia confronts the men who killed one of their brothers.

metas.name: S-21: The Khmer Rouge Killing Machine
metas.description:
Captures atrocity recalled as office procedure: survivor Vann Nath brings former Tuol Sleng guards back into the prison, where they re-enact their daily routines of shackling and paperwork and find nothing dramatic in their own memories.

A unique documentary on the notorious S-21 prison, today the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, with testimony by the only surviving prisoners and former Khmer Rouge guards.

metas.name: Cameraperson
metas.description:
Captures a career of looking, reckoned with: Kirsten Johnson cuts decades of outtakes from other people's difficult documentaries — Bosnia, Darfur, her own mother's decline — into a memoir about what pointing a camera at someone's worst day costs.

Exposing her role behind the camera, Kirsten Johnson reaches into the vast trove of footage she has shot over decades around the world. What emerges is a visually bold memoir and a revelatory interrogation of the power of the camera.

metas.name: The Battle of Chile
metas.description:
Captures a revolution and its destruction filmed by people unsure which they were recording: Guzmán's crew shoots Allende's final year in Chile's streets across three parts, as mass rallies and strikes give way to the coup arriving around the camera.

The chronicle of the political tension in Chile in 1973 and of the violent counter revolution against the democratically elected government of Salvador Allende.

metas.name: The Salt of the Earth
metas.description:
Captures what a lifetime of looking at suffering does to a person, and one answer to it. Photographer Sebastião Salgado walks through forty years of famine, war and exodus in his own images, then turns to restoring a dead forest — and it works.

The life and work of photographer Sebastião Salgado, who has spent forty years documenting societies in hidden corners of the world.

metas.name: The Farthest
metas.description:
Captures the most optimistic object our species has ever made, and the scientists ageing alongside it. The Voyager probes, told by the people who built them, carrying a golden record of human greetings out of the solar system.

It is one of humankind's greatest achievements. More than 12 billion miles away a tiny spaceship is leaving our Solar System and entering the void of deep space - the first human-made object ever to do so.

metas.name: The Atomic Cafe
metas.director: Jayne Loader, Kevin Rafferty, Pierce Rafferty
metas.description:
Captures a state lying to its citizens in its own cheerful voice. Nothing but 1940s–50s American government films, ads and newsreels about the bomb, cut together with no narration: duck and cover, soldiers reassured about fallout.

Disturbing collection of 1940s and 1950s United States government-issued propaganda films designed to reassure Americans that the atomic bomb was not a threat to their safety.

metas.name: They Shall Not Grow Old
metas.description:
Captures the trenches suddenly populated by recognisable young men instead of ghosts. Peter Jackson restores jerky silent WWI footage to correct speed, colourises it, and adds voices reconstructed from veterans' interviews and lip-reading.

A documentary about World War I with never-before-seen footage to commemorate the centennial of the end of the war.

metas.name: A Film Unfinished
metas.description:
Captures how a fabricated archive keeps passing as truth until someone watches it slowly enough. A Nazi propaganda film shot in the Warsaw Ghetto is taken apart shot by shot, including outtakes where the staging shows.

A film about an unfinished film which portrays the people behind and before the camera in the Warsaw Ghetto, exposing the extent of the cinematic manipulation forever changing the way we look at historic images.

metas.name: Winter on Fire: Ukraine's Fight for Freedom
metas.description:
Captures a protest becoming a revolution in real time, and what it costs the people who refuse to leave. Kyiv's Euromaidan over 93 days, from student demonstration to a government shooting its own citizens, filmed inside the square.

A documentary on the unrest in Ukraine during 2013 and 2014, as student demonstrations supporting European integration grew into a violent revolution calling for the resignation of President Viktor F. Yanukovich.

metas.name: 13th
metas.description:
Captures the essay-documentary at maximum force — a thesis you can feel being assembled. DuVernay builds one chain from the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause through convict leasing, Jim Crow and the war on drugs to mass incarceration.

An in-depth look at the prison system in the United States and how it reveals the nation's history of racial inequality.

metas.name: Won't You Be My Neighbor?
metas.description:
Captures gentleness deployed as a discipline, not a temperament. Fred Rogers turns out to have been exactly as radical as he appeared: using children's television to insist, slowly and on purpose, that every child is lovable as they are.

An exploration of the life, lessons, and legacy of iconic children's television host Fred Rogers.

metas.name: Tim's Vermeer
metas.description:
Captures obsession as method: an engineering argument settled by actually doing the thing. Inventor Tim Jenison, who can't paint, spends years testing his theory that Vermeer used optical devices — by building the device and painting a Vermeer with it.

Inventor Tim Jenison seeks to understand the painting techniques used by Dutch Master Johannes Vermeer.

metas.name: Primary
metas.description:
Captures the moment politics and television fused, visible as it happens. The film that invented American cinéma vérité: newly portable sync-sound cameras follow Kennedy and Humphrey through the 1960 Wisconsin primary, into rooms no camera had entered before.

Cinéma vérité feature that follows presidential hopefuls John F. Kennedy and Hubert H. Humphrey during the 1960 Wisconsin primary.

metas.name: Andrei Rublev
metas.description:
Captures an artist trying to make images of faith in a world of mud and violence. Medieval Russia through its greatest icon painter: raids, pagan festivals, and a boy casting a bell he may not know how to cast.

The life, times and afflictions of the fifteenth-century Russian iconographer St. Andrei Rublev.

metas.name: Pirosmani
metas.description:
Captures a film learning to see the way its subject painted. Georgian folk painter Niko Pirosmani's life built from his own canvases — taverns, feasts, animals, a man painting signs for food and dying unrecognised.

A biography of the Georgian primitive artist Nikoloz Pirosmanishvili (1862–1918), better known as Pirosmani, who died of starvation and sold his paintings to bars and restaurants for food and drink. The film experiments with color control techniques based on the painter’s style.

metas.name: Marketa Lazarová
metas.description:
Captures a whole civilisation changing gods. Medieval Bohemia in deep winter — pagan and Christian clans, wolf packs, kidnapped nuns, mud and chanting — with Shadows' savage lyricism stretched to epic scale. Frequently called the greatest Czech film.

A grim portrayal of the shift from Paganism to Christianity in medieval central Europe - as a young virgin promised to God is kidnapped and raped by a marauder who her religious father seeks to kill in return.

metas.name: The Round-Up
metas.description:
Captures power as folk dance. On an endless white plain, authorities process prisoners from a peasant uprising through rituals of selection and betrayal, in Jancsó's choreographed long takes — nobody's psychology is explained, and the rituals are the point.

In Hungary, the national movement led by Kossuth has been crushed and the Austrian hegemony re-established, but partisans carry on with violent actions. In order to root out the guerilla, the army rounds up suspects and jails them...

metas.name: Pather Panchali
metas.description:
Captures lyricism at ground level. Ray's Bengal village childhood — Apu and his sister Durga, the monsoon arriving like a miracle — where poverty is filmed as a complete sensory world rather than a condition to be pitied.

Impoverished priest Harihar Ray, dreaming of a better life for himself and his family, leaves his rural Bengal village in search of work.

metas.name: The Leopard
metas.description:
Captures pageantry as an instrument for measuring decay. Visconti's Sicilian prince watches his class dissolve during Italian unification, and the film saves its greatest set piece for a 45-minute ball where the old world dances beautifully with the one replacing it.

The Prince of Salina, a noble aristocrat of impeccable integrity, tries to preserve his family and class amid the tumultuous social upheavals of 1860s Sicily.

metas.name: Caravaggio
metas.description:
Captures a film thinking in paintings the way The Colour of Pomegranates does, but grubbier, queerer, and made for almost no money. Jarman stages the painter's life as living versions of his canvases, with calculators and motorbikes left sitting in the 1600s.

A retelling of the life of the celebrated 17th-century painter through his brilliant, nearly blasphemous paintings and his flirtations with the underworld.

metas.name: Yellow Earth
metas.description:
Captures a folk culture so total it becomes the cinematography. A Communist soldier arrives in a loess-plateau village in 1939 to collect folk songs for the army, and finds a girl whose singing is the only free thing in her life.

A communist soldier is sent to a remote region of China in order to collect folk songs. Staying with a peasant family (a widower with two small children), he discovers a community whose way of life is completely alien to him, but he gradually wins their trust.

metas.name: Zama
metas.description:
Captures empire as a man rotting in a landscape that was never his and barely notices him. Martel strands a Spanish colonial officer in a Paraguayan backwater, waiting years for a transfer that never comes, while insects, water and distant animals become the real film.

Don Diego de Zama is a Spanish officer of the seventeenth century settled in Asunción, who awaits his transfer to Buenos Aires.

metas.name: The Travelling Players
metas.description:
Captures a nation's history carried by the people paid to keep entertaining it. Angelopoulos follows a folk theatre troupe performing the same pastoral play across Greece from 1939 to 1952, and in vast single takes, occupation, civil war and executions slide past mid-scene.

Greece, 1939-1952: Fascist, Nazi, and Communist conflict, as seen through the eyes of a family of travelling provincial players.

metas.name: The Tree of Wooden Clogs
metas.description:
Captures the folk world at the opposite end of the temperament scale from Parajanov — patient, plain, and quietly overwhelming. Olmi films Lombardy peasants playing their grandparents' generation: four families, one farm, a whole year of seasons, labour and ritual.

Peasant life in a feudal farm in rural Italy at the end of the 19th century.
